response.initial_request: The washer-dryer displays error E13. The tenant has tried draining the water, but the appliance still does not work.

other_sections.Attachments: No attachments are available for this case.

events.body: Acknowledged the report and said the landlord's approval would be sought before arranging work.
Asked the tenant to provide the appliance brand, model, E-number and serial number shown on its identification label.
Replied without the requested appliance identification details.
Said they would contact their insurer to sort out the appliance.
Asked whether the tenant could still use the machine despite the error, saying this information was requested while arranging an engineer.
Asked whether the machine remained usable or was completely out of service.
The tenant confirmed the machine was unusable and the error appeared when they tried to operate it. They asked for a prompt resolution and said the household had laundry waiting.
Said they would inform the engineer and asked about a preferred attendance time.
Said the tenant worked from home and could accommodate a visit on any day, asking for a specific day and morning or afternoon window once available.

Reported that the insurer had approved a repair and asked Northbridge Lettings to contact the insurer or repair provider to arrange it. The landlord said they were abroad and unable to make the arrangements themselves.

Told the tenant that the landlord had authorized a repair through the manufacturer's service arrangement and instructed the tenant to contact the manufacturer's service desk directly to book a convenient engineer visit. The message said the appliance identification details, including its model and serial information, might be required and should be available when calling.
Said Northbridge Lettings was preparing to schedule an inspection and requested possible appointment windows and the appliance identification details.

Said someone was generally home but requested at least three hours' notice. The tenant expressed frustration with the delay and described doing laundry by hand. The requested appliance identification details were not included.
Reported that the repair provider could not find the relevant account or order under the landlord's name and asked for the purchase name, email, or order reference.
Said the repair provider would not book without the appliance's E-number and serial number, and asked Northbridge Lettings to obtain those details from the tenant.
Said the appliance identification details requested in the previous email had not arrived.
Supplied the appliance identification details in the body of the email. No booking confirmation was included.

Reported that an engineer had been booked for 9 September between 12:00 and 17:00. The landlord said the engineer would call before arrival and that they would pass on notice. No booking confirmation was included.
Passed on the reported 9 September appointment window and asked that someone be available for access.
Acknowledged the appointment details with a brief thank-you.
Said the engineer had called and would be at the property within about 20 minutes to fix the machine. This is an expected visit, not confirmation of an inspection or repair outcome.
Asked whether the engineer had attended and whether the appliance was working.
Said a replacement washing machine was needed and asked whether a unit described as 825 cm high would fit; the previous machine was described as 820 cm.
Asked the tenant to measure the available space in millimetres and note any other fitting constraints, referring to the proposed unit height as 825 mm.

Estimated the available height at about 835 mm and said an 825 mm unit should fit. The tenant described the existing appliance as integrated and fixed to the cabinet door; the rear connections could not be checked without moving it.

Passed on the tenant's approximate 835 mm measurement and the integrated-unit constraint, noting that rear connections had not been inspected. Asked how the landlord wished to proceed with ordering and installation.
Said a new washing machine had been ordered, with delivery timing to follow. The landlord said installers would fit it and take the old unit away for disposal.
Requested a quote for removal and replacement of the washing machine.
Said they had sorted it and arranged delivery, setup, and disposal of the old machine. They complained that the response had taken too long. No delivery or installation date was provided.
When asked about delivery, the tenant said no replacement had arrived and there was no packaging at the property.

Replied to a maintenance follow-up: “Yes, the job is completed.” In the same message, said they had received another email about a planned washing-machine change and asked whether it was still happening.

args.reason: Landlord complained about delay (event 29), and the record contradicts itself on whether the work is done and whether a replacement is happening (events 29, 30, 31). One message would not settle it.

handover_note.known: Case property: 8 Brackenmere Walk, Vellumford, ZZ1 1ZZ. Washer-dryer showed error E13 and was unusable (events 1, 7). The landlord said the insurer approved a repair (event 10). The landlord reported an engineer booked for 9 Sept (event 18) and said the engineer was about to arrive (event 21). There is no engineer report or booking confirmation. On 14 Sept the landlord said a replacement was needed (event 23). On 19 Sept the landlord said a new machine was ordered (event 27). On 21 Sept the landlord asked for a quote for removal and replacement (event 28). The same day the landlord said they had sorted delivery, setup and disposal, and complained the response took too long (event 29).
handover_note.conflicts: 1) On 24 Sept the tenant said no replacement had arrived and there was no packaging (event 30). On 25 Sept the tenant replied 'Yes, the job is completed' to a follow-up. In the same message the tenant asked whether a planned washing-machine change was still happening (event 31). It is unclear whether the job is complete, and the tenant seems to have misread the follow-up. 2) Event 28 asks the agency for a quote, but event 29 says the landlord had already arranged it themselves. 3) There is no evidence the engineer attended on 9 Sept, and no evidence of the insurer's repair outcome. 4) The landlord's height figures are given as 825 cm and 820 cm (event 23), against 825 mm in event 24, so the unit of measure is inconsistent. 5) The tenant never supplied the appliance identification details (events 3, 13). Event 17 says they were supplied to the landlord, but the source is unclear. 6) Event 11 told the tenant to book the manufacturer's engineer themselves, while the landlord was booking one (event 18).
handover_note.done: No messages sent and no bookings made. I only reviewed the record. No contractor was instructed and no invoice or charge exists.
handover_note.needed: Property manager to: 1) Reply to the landlord's complaint about delay (event 29). 2) Confirm with the landlord the delivery and installation date and who is installing. 3) Confirm with the tenant whether the washer-dryer has been replaced or fixed, and answer their question in event 31. 4) Decide whether the quote requested in event 28 is still needed. 5) Don't close the case until completion is evidenced.

args.summary: Escalated to the property manager. The landlord complained about delay, and the record contradicts itself on whether the job is done and whether a replacement washing machine is coming.
facts: The landlord complained that the response took too long (event 29).
The tenant said on 24 Sept that no replacement had arrived and there was no packaging (event 30).
On 25 Sept the tenant said 'the job is completed' but also asked whether a planned washing-machine change was still happening (event 31).
The landlord said a new machine was ordered and delivery, setup and disposal were arranged, with no date given (events 27, 29).
The landlord asked for a quote on 21 Sept (event 28) but said the same day they had sorted it themselves (event 29).
The 9 Sept engineer visit has no confirmed outcome (events 18, 21, 22).
conflicts: Event 31 says the job is completed, but event 30 says nothing was delivered and event 31 asks if the change is still happening.
Event 28 asks the agency for a quote, but event 29 says the landlord had already arranged the replacement.
Event 23 gives the unit height in cm and event 24 gives it in mm.
There is no evidence the engineer attended, and the replacement plan appeared without any recorded repair outcome.
missing: Delivery and installation date and installer
Confirmation of whether the washer-dryer is now working or replaced
Appliance identification details from the tenant
options_rejected: Ask the tenant to confirm completion: the landlord has complained about delay, and the landlord's and tenant's accounts conflict, so one message would not settle it.
Close the case: there is no evidence of completion, and the tenant's own message contradicts it.
Wait: the landlord has complained about delay, and the playbook says to escalate.
args.uncertainty: The tenant's 'job completed' reply (event 31) may refer to a different follow-up, so I can't tell whether the machine has been replaced.
